text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they often add it to a shared project. A CI system then automatically creates a build of the software. This means it checks that all the parts work together correctly. Next, the system runs automated tests to find any problems. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious. A CI pipeline is the series of steps that runs these builds and tests. By using CI pipelines, teams can quickly find and fix bugs, which leads to better and more reliable software.
